name: deriv_synthetic_indices.json
description: Deriv synthetic instruments: volatility indices, drift switching indices (DSI 10/20/30) and other synthetics, with regime structure, strategies and product notes. Educational; verify current specs on deriv.com.
what_it_is: Synthetic price series generated by an algorithm with a fixed annualised volatility (e.g. V75 = 75%). Not the CBOE VIX. Trades 24/7, no news, earnings or macro events. Deriv is the counterparty on CFDs.
not_to_confuse: CBOE VIX measures implied volatility of S&P 500 options. Deriv Volatility Indices are simulated prices, not a measure of fear in a real market.

index_table.best_for: Small size, advanced risk control only

index_table.character: A new tick every second; more ticks, smaller individual moves
A tick every 2 seconds; fewer, larger ticks

core_principles.text: Each index has a different typical range, tick behaviour and stop-out frequency. A setup tuned for V10 is likely too slow for V75 and too noisy for V250. Re-test parameters per index.
Higher volatility does not mean easier profit. It means bigger stops, smaller position size and faster losses.
Before entry classify the chart as trending, ranging, expanding or contracting, and use the matching method.
Risk 0.25-1% per trade (hard cap 2%), daily cap 3-5%, weekly cap 8-10%, always a predefined stop.
Master one index and one setup for at least 90 days of demo/small-live before adding others.

Because prices come from an algorithm with no order book, Deriv states that historic patterns can be coincidental. Treat all indicator strategies below as hypotheses to be validated by tests in 08_backtesting_and_validation.json, not as proven edges.

strategies.name: Trend-following pullback
strategies.concept: Trade with the dominant trend after a pullback, not at the extended end of a move.
long_rules: Price above EMA50 and EMA200.
EMA20 above EMA50.
Price pulls back toward EMA20 or EMA50.
Bullish rejection candle (pin bar, engulfing, or strong close back above EMA).
Enter on candle close or small break above signal-candle high.
Stop below pullback swing low with ATR buffer.
Target prior high; trail stop after 1R.
strategies.short_rules: Mirror of long: price below EMA50/EMA200, EMA20 below EMA50, pullback into EMA20/50, bearish rejection candle, stop above pullback high, target prior low or trail after 1R.
no_trade: price closed beyond EMA50 against trend
stop distance makes RR below minimum
tests: Compare with random-entry baseline using same exits

strategies.name: Breakout-retest continuation
strategies.concept: After compression, wait for a structure break and enter on retest instead of chasing.
steps: Find a horizontal level tested at least twice.
Wait for a strong candle close beyond the level.
Wait for pullback to the broken level.
Enter when retest holds and a continuation candle forms.
Stop beyond retest wick or recent swing.
Target next structure level or measured move.
valid_filters: Candle range or tick activity expands
Retest does not close back inside old range
Price has not already run more than 1.5-2 ATR from breakout point
invalid_signs: Many candles stuck at the level

strategies.name: Range mean reversion
strategies.concept: Buy support, sell resistance inside a confirmed range and target midpoint or opposite side.
long_rules: Sideways range confirmed
Price touches/pierces lower band
RSI below 30 or bullish divergence
Bullish reversal candle
Enter on close
Stop below range low plus ATR buffer
Target midpoint first, then upper boundary
strategies.short_rules: Mirror at upper band and range high.
strategies.critical_warning: Never mean-revert in a strong trend. If EMA20 and EMA50 are widely separated or price keeps making higher highs/lower lows, band touches are continuation signals.

strategies.name: EMA ribbon momentum (8/21/50 + Stochastic)
long_rules: EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA50
Pullback to EMA8 or EMA21
Stochastic rises from below 20 or crosses up
Bullish candle closes above EMA8
Enter long
Stop below swing low or 1 ATR
Exit at 1.5-2R or when EMA8 crosses below EMA21
strategies.short_rules: Mirror: EMA8 < EMA21 < EMA50, pullback up, Stochastic falls from above 80, bearish close below EMA8, stop above swing high or 1 ATR, exit 1.5-2R or bearish cross.

strategies.name: Multi-timeframe confluence
rules: Determine H4 bias: bullish, bearish, neutral.
On H1 find pullback into EMA, demand/supply zone or structure level.
On M15 wait for change of character: bullish = break of minor lower high; bearish = break of minor higher low.
Enter only in H4/H1 direction.
Stop beyond M15 invalidation point.
Target next H1 structure level.
strategies.example: V75 long: H4 above EMA200 and bullish; H1 pullback to EMA50 and old resistance-turned-support; M15 bullish engulfing after sweep of a minor low; enter at M15 close; stop below sweep low; target previous H1 high; risk 1%.

strategies.name: Volatility-scaled position sizing
strategies.formula: size = (equity * risk%) / stop_distance; stop_distance = k * ATR14
strategies.example: Equity 1000, risk 1% = 10, stop distance 10 points => 1 unit per point.
strategies.rule: Never use the same lot size across V10, V75 and V250.

strategies.name: Time/session filtering and personal stats
strategies.text: Synthetics run 24/7, so session effects come from you (fatigue, focus), not from the market. Trade a fixed 1-2 hour window, log performance by hour and by index, and keep only windows with positive expectancy over 100+ trades.

strategies.name: Bollinger/Keltner squeeze breakout (additional)
rules: Detect squeeze: Bollinger Bands(20,2) inside Keltner(20, 1.5*ATR) or band width at 20-bar low.
Wait for a close outside the bands with expanding candle range.
Enter in breakout direction on close or small pullback.
Stop at opposite side of squeeze or 1.5 ATR.
Trail with EMA20 or 2 ATR.
strategies.filter: Skip if the breakout candle is already more than 2 ATR long (late entry).

strategies.name: Donchian channel breakout (additional)
rules: Long on close above highest high of last N bars (N=20 on M15/H1).
Exit on close below lowest low of last N/2 bars or trailing 2-3 ATR stop.
Risk 0.5% per trade, expect low win rate (30-45%) with larger winners.
Only trade when ADX > 20.
strategies.note: Test whether the generator's behaviour gives any trend persistence at all; if random-walk-like, expect no edge after costs.

product_selection.notes: Leverage and stops required; swaps for overnight; Deriv is counterparty.
Understand payout, expiry, knock-out, financing before use.

trading_plan_template.market: One index only for first 90 days. Gentle option: V10/V25 on H4. Common choice: V75 on H1.
entry_checklist_long: Price pulled back to EMA20/50 or support
exit_rules: Move stop to breakeven after 1R (test whether it helps)
Trail behind EMA20 or swing points
Close fully at 2-3R or when structure breaks

common_mistakes: Over-leveraging V100/V250 instead of shrinking size.
Using fixed lot sizes regardless of stop distance.
Trading every candle without a defined setup.
Switching strategies after 5 losses instead of judging 50-100 trades.
Ignoring spread and slippage on fast indices.
Revenge trading; stop for the day after two consecutive losses.
Trading too many indices at once.

progression_plan.task: Demo V10/V25 on H1/H4; learn execution, stops, sizing.
Backtest 100 trend-pullback trades on one index.
Forward-test on demo with fixed rules and journal.
Raise size only if profit factor > 1.3 and drawdown acceptable.
Add V75/V100 only after consistency on lower-volatility indices.

bottom_line: Most defensible approach: small risk, ATR-based stops, multi-timeframe filter, one index, strict testing. No method guarantees profit; synthetic indices are algorithmic and the broker takes the other side.

drift_switch_indices.instrument_family: Deriv Drift Switch Indices (DSI 10, DSI 20, DSI 30)
drift_switch_indices.what_it_is: CFD on a synthetic, algorithmically generated index that switches between three regimes. Quotes come from cryptographically secure random numbers; news and order flow do not drive price; Deriv is the counterparty.

regimes.name: Driftless (sideways)
regimes.response: Stand aside or range-trade cautiously with small targets

switch_interval.meaning: The number in the name is the AVERAGE time between regime switches: DSI 10 about 10 minutes, DSI 20 about 20, DSI 30 about 30.
switch_interval.warning: It is an average, not a countdown. Switches can occur earlier or later. Do not time trades to an exact minute.

drift_switch_indices.core_edge: Regime persistence: enter after a regime is confirmed and exit before its average duration is exhausted. Indicators only help confirm the regime; the structural edge is the designed drift.
timing_rules: Enter after confirmation, not at the guessed switch moment.

Avoid entering late in a regime; if most of the average duration has elapsed, the remaining edge is weaker (but remember switching is random so there may be no true 'aging' effect; test whether elapsed time actually predicts anything on your data).
Beginner choice: DSI 30, since it switches less often and gives more analysis time.

strategies.name: Regime-following system

setup.charts: M1/M5 for DSI 10; M5 for DSI 20; M5/M15 for DSI 30

long_rules: Price above both EMA20 and EMA50.
EMA20 above EMA50.
Higher highs and higher lows.
Enter on pullback to EMA20 or after bullish breakout candle closes.
Stop below recent swing low or 1.5-2 ATR.
Take profit before expected regime duration ends (e.g. DSI 10 long exits after about 6-8 minutes if target met).
strategies.short_rules: Mirror: price below both EMAs, EMA20 below EMA50, lower highs/lows, pullback short or breakdown candle, stop above swing high or 1.5-2 ATR, exit before regime duration exhausted.
no_trade_rules: Candles have long wicks on both sides.
Trend has run close to the full average switch interval.
Last two same-direction trades were stopped out: pause and reassess.

strategies.name: Stop-and-reverse
strategies.description: Close a long when the bullish regime weakens, then consider a short only if a bearish regime confirms.
rules: Open long only after bullish confirmation.
If price closes below EMA20 and then EMA50, close the long.
Do not instantly reverse. Require lower high, strong bearish close and price below both EMAs.
If unclear, stay flat; the sideways regime is a valid outcome.
Cycle: long -> exit on trend break -> wait -> short only on confirmed bearish regime -> exit -> wait.
strategies.warning: Forcing reversals during driftless phases is a common account killer.

strategies.name: Range trading in driftless phases
rules: Mark latest clear swing high and low on M5/M15.
Buy near support only with bullish rejection and no broken structure.
Sell near resistance only with bearish rejection and no broken structure.
Use tighter targets than trend trades.
If price closes beyond range with momentum, stop range trading and switch to regime-following.

strategies.name: Two-timeframe confirmation
strategies.example: DSI 30: if M15 is clearly bullish take only long setups on M5; if M15 flat or conflicting, reduce size or wait.

strategies.name: Statistical regime detection (additional, testable)
strategies.idea: Estimate drift directly instead of relying only on EMAs.
method: Rolling mean of returns over N bars (e.g. N=12 on M1 for DSI 10) divided by (stdev/sqrt(N)) gives a t-statistic of drift.
t > +2: bullish regime likely; t < -2: bearish; |t| < 1: driftless.
Optionally use CUSUM or a Hidden Markov Model with 3 states fitted on returns.
Backtest entry delay vs regime age to see how quickly the detector confirms a switch; detection lag eats part of the regime.
strategies.note: Because drift is small relative to noise, detection is slow and noisy; measure the realised hit rate before trading it.

strategies.name: Test whether regime age matters (additional)
strategies.text: If switch times are memoryless (exponential-like), remaining expected duration does not shrink with age, so 'exit because it is old' would have no basis. If they are not memoryless, age matters. Collect many regimes from historical ticks, estimate the duration distribution, and test it before building rules on age.

risk_management.risk_classification: Deriv rates DSI CFDs at its highest risk class (7 of 7); losses can exceed expectations if unmanaged.
rules: Risk 0.25-1% of equity per trade (maximum 1%).
Always place stop before entry.
Daily loss limit 2-3%; stop when hit.
One or two correlated DSI positions at most.
Never increase size after losses.
Avoid overnight holds if swap cost is material (Deriv KID example: 7.5% annual swap on DSI 10; verify current).
Spread is paid each round trip; frequent scalping can turn a marginal idea into a loser.
risk_management.position_size_example: Equity 1000, risk 1% = 10. Stop 50 index points. Choose lot size so 50 points = 10 currency units; check broker value per point; never pick lot first.

what_to_avoid: Digit or binary-style systems on DSI (edge is directional regime persistence).
Trusting indicators more than risk control.
practical_playbook: Trade one DSI only; start with DSI 30.
Wait for EMA alignment plus pullback.
Exit before the average regime duration is exhausted.
Stop after 2-3 losses or a 2-3% daily loss.
Demo test at least 100 trades before real money.
drift_switch_indices.reality_check: No strategy guarantees profit on DSI. It is synthetic and random-number driven; past behaviour does not ensure future results. Treat as short-term, high-risk speculation; prioritise capital preservation over trade frequency.

other_synthetic_indices.note: Based on Deriv product descriptions found in research plus general knowledge. Product specs change; the app should tell users to verify on deriv.com.
other_synthetic_indices.global_warning: Deriv states that most synthetic indices have no order book, so apparent historical patterns can be coincidental, and technical indicators are most suitable on Range Break indices. Approach every strategy here as a testable hypothesis.

instruments.name: Crash and Boom indices
facts: Crash indices generate sudden downward spikes with a gradual upward drift between spikes.
Boom indices generate sudden upward spikes with a gradual downward drift between spikes.
The number (e.g. 50, 150, 300, 500, 600, 900, 1000) is the average number of ticks between spikes. Lower number = more frequent, typically smaller impact per spike; higher number = rarer.
Available on Deriv MT5 and cTrader as CFDs, and via Deriv Trader/Deriv Bot as Multipliers and Accumulators.
instruments.beginner_tip: Lower numbers such as 150 or 300 give more frequent spikes with smaller volatility between them and are usually considered friendlier to learn on.

strategies.name: Trade with the slow drift, expect a spike against you
strategies.text: On Boom the drift between spikes is down; on Crash it is up. A spike against your position is the main risk. Sizing and stops must assume a spike can gap through your stop.
rules: Use small size so a full spike against you stays within the risk cap.
Remember a stop can be skipped by a spike so real loss may exceed planned loss.

strategies.name: Spike catching (trade in spike direction)
strategies.text: Enter in the spike direction (long Boom, short Crash) with a tiny size and tight time stop, aiming for the next spike. Each spike has roughly 1/N probability per tick (N = index number), so expected waiting time is about N ticks, and the arrival is memoryless: being 'overdue' does not raise probability.
strategies.math: P(no spike in k ticks) = (1 - 1/N)^k. Example N=1000: after 1000 ticks the chance of no spike is about 37%.
strategies.warning: Holding for a spike while drift moves against you means many small losses; compute expectancy including drift and costs. Do not assume a spike is 'due'. That is the gambler's fallacy.

strategies.name: Post-spike drift trade
strategies.text: After a spike, trade the slow drift direction (up after Crash spike, down after Boom spike) with defined stop; exit before the next possible spike or use tiny size.
strategies.tests: Measure average return in the N ticks after a spike versus all other ticks.

strategies.name: Accumulators on Crash/Boom
strategies.text: Accumulators grow stake per tick while price stays inside a barrier; spikes typically knock them out. Calculate expected value using spike frequency and growth rate before use.

instruments.name: Step Index
facts: Price moves in fixed-size steps up or down each tick with equal probability (a symmetric random walk with constant step size).
instruments.implication: Technical analysis edge is doubtful because moves are symmetric random steps; the main considerations are spread cost and risk control.

strategies.name: Probability-based sizing only
strategies.text: Use random-walk math for expected distance: typical move after n ticks scales with sqrt(n) steps. Set stops/targets in multiples of step size with costs considered.

instruments.name: Skew Step indices
facts: Asymmetric steps and probabilities: small moves occur with 80% or 90% probability and large moves with 10% or 20% probability.
instruments.implication: The skew creates a positive or negative drift between rare large moves, similar in spirit to Crash/Boom but with step mechanics.

strategies.name: Expected value per tick calculation
strategies.text: Compute EV = p_small*step_small + p_large*step_large (with signs) and compare with spread to see if a directional bias survives costs.

instruments.name: Multi Step indices
facts: Variants with multiple step sizes per tick (check Deriv's current spec).
instruments.implication: Treat like random-step instruments; verify parameters in official docs before building rules.

instruments.name: Jump indices
facts: Constant base volatility with occasional large jumps up or down at random intervals (check Deriv spec for jump frequency and size).

strategies.name: Jump-aware sizing
strategies.text: Plan for gap-through-stop events. Use smaller size, avoid tight stops that jumps will skip, and avoid holding multiple open positions simultaneously.

instruments.name: Range Break indices
facts: Price oscillates between a support and a resistance level, then breaks out at random times; Deriv notes technical analysis and channel analysis may be more useful here than on other synthetics.

strategies.name: Channel trading with breakout awareness
rules: Mark upper and lower boundaries from repeated touches.
Fade reversals near edges with stops just beyond the boundary.
If a candle closes beyond the boundary with strong range, stop fading; treat as break and either stand aside or trade retest continuation.
Measure how far past the old boundary price typically runs after a break and use that for targets.
strategies.tests: Record range duration, break frequency and post-break run distance on thousands of ticks; derive stops/targets from those numbers.

instruments.name: DEX indices (and similar newer synthetics)
facts: Directional-bias style indices (e.g. DEX 600/900/1500 up or down) with recurring spikes in one direction and drift in the other; check Deriv docs for the exact design.
instruments.implication: Handle like Crash/Boom: small size, spike awareness, test expected value.

instruments.name: Hybrid, Daily Reset, Basket indices
facts: Other Deriv synthetic families exist (e.g. daily reset indices, Forex/commodity baskets, Vol over Crash/Boom hybrids). Specs change.
instruments.implication: Before trading any new index, read its official spec: tick frequency, volatility, spike or regime parameters, costs, margin.

how_to_approach_any_new_synthetic: Read the official spec and identify the designed behaviour (drift, spike frequency, step size, regime switching, range breaks).
Download tick/candle history and measure that behaviour: spike counts, return distribution, autocorrelation, regime lengths.
Test for autocorrelation of returns (Ljung-Box), Hurst exponent (about 0.5 = random walk), and variance ratio test. If all look random, indicator strategies likely have no edge.
Build only strategies tied to a measurable structural feature.
Walk-forward and forward test small before scaling.

statistical_checks.name: Autocorrelation of returns
statistical_checks.meaning: Significant positive = trend persistence; negative = mean reversion; near zero = random walk.

statistical_checks.name: Hurst exponent
statistical_checks.meaning: H > 0.5 trending, H = 0.5 random, H < 0.5 mean-reverting.

statistical_checks.name: Variance ratio test (Lo-MacKinlay)
statistical_checks.meaning: Ratio different from 1 across horizons suggests non-random behaviour.

statistical_checks.name: Runs test
statistical_checks.meaning: Compares observed streaks against random expectation.

statistical_checks.name: Distribution of spike gaps
statistical_checks.meaning: Check if gaps are geometric/exponential (memoryless) or have structure.
